provenance.assertion: NO document body was generated, summarised, paraphrased or invented by an AI or by a human, and no sentence was added between API values. Every character of every `text` field is either an API field name (used as a line label) or a value taken from the stored raw API response. Two body styles exist and are declared per document in `text_style`: (1) 'prose' - the source's own prose fields are concatenated in a fixed order and separated by blank lines (header labels are API field names); (2) 'field_value_rendering' - a `field: value` rendering used only for 510(k) and PMA records, which contain no prose. The only transformations applied are whitespace normalisation (intra-line runs collapsed, original paragraph breaks kept) and truncation at a sentence boundary when assembled text exceeded 3000 characters (flagged text_truncated=true). Every date and URL in this manifest comes from the API responses recorded under raw/.
provenance.assembly_rule: prose: header_lines + blank line + prose values in fixed order separated by blank lines (+ structured tail if prose < 800 chars, offset recorded in structured_tail_starts_at_char); field_value_rendering: newline-join of f'{api.field.path}: {value}' in a fixed documented order; content_sha256 = sha256(text utf-8), raw_sha256 = sha256(stored raw record file bytes); text_fields lists the contributing API field paths in order

http.retry_policy: up to 3 attempts, exponential back-off on 403/429/5xx
http.user_agent: MedRadar-corpus-collector/1.0 (academic event-extraction research; polite rate-limited client)

raw_storage.record_file: raw/<source>/<doc_id>.json - the chosen API record object
raw_storage.pool_response: raw/_pools/<query>.json - exact HTTP body of each search query
raw_storage.verification_response: raw/_verifications/<doc_id>.json - exact HTTP body of the record-level URL check

provenance.entity_attribution_policy: Attribution uses the verbatim entity string from the API record, matched against an explicit per-company prefix allowlist; the verbatim string is stored per document in entity_string_verbatim. GE HealthCare is restricted to 'GE Healthcare'/'GE HealthCare' strings and explicitly excludes legacy 'GE Medical Systems'/'General Electric'. Dräger records are matched on the ASCII 'Draeger' because openFDA rejects non-ASCII terms with HTTP 400 (probe recorded in failures) and are Drägerwerk corporate entities. Siemens Healthineers includes legacy 'Siemens Medical ...' entities by corporate lineage, flagged per document in notes.

failures.recovery: ASCII transliteration 'Draeger' used for all Dräger queries; this is a documented API constraint, not a source block

known_limitations: TEXT REALISM: documents with text_style='prose' are assembled from the record's own prose fields (ClinicalTrials.gov official title / brief summary / detailed description / eligibility criteria; FDA recall reason / product description / action / distribution / code info). They are NOT press releases, peer-reviewed papers, complete FDA enforcement reports or full study protocols, and must not be described as such. Documents with text_style='field_value_rendering' (510(k) clearances and PMA approvals) are key-value renderings of a tabular API record because those records contain essentially no prose, so they are not prose documents at all.
The prose fields used are sponsor-authored or firm-authored regulatory statements; they can be formulaic and legally hedged, so event density per document is lower than in press releases or papers.
The short header block at the top of a prose document uses the API's own field names as labels; it is structure, not narrative, and is not part of the prose body.

Prose fields are assembled in a fixed order before the 3000-character cap is applied; when a registration's detailedDescription is long, eligibilityCriteria is assembled but removed by truncation. Each affected document lists those fields in notes as 'removed by the 3000-character truncation' and in the prose_fields_dropped note, so no content is silently misrepresented as absent from the source.

Raw record files are the individual record objects serialised as JSON (indent=2, UTF-8); the exact HTTP response bytes of every query and every record-level verification are preserved separately under raw/_pools/ and raw/_verifications/.
Record selection is deterministic for a fixed API snapshot, but openFDA and ClinicalTrials.gov are live databases: --refresh may select different records if the underlying data changes.
openFDA answers a query with no matches using HTTP 404 (not an empty 200 payload); such cases are recorded under zero_result_queries, not as failures.
Document counts per company differ because a candidate must both match the entity allowlist and yield 800-3000 characters of verbatim field text from a single API record.

PMA approval records are mostly tabular supplements; only the ao_statement (approval-order statement) carries semi-prose and it is kept inside the field:value rendering rather than being dressed up as a document.
